questions.question: _____, is situated high aloft a hill called Neelachal Parbat or Kamagiri in the city of Guwahati.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kamakhya Temple**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kamakhya Temple** is **situated high aloft a hill called Neelachal Parbat or Kamagiri **in the city of **Guwahati**, which is in the northeastern state of Assam, India.
 
• It is a renowned Hindu temple dedicated to the** goddess Kamakhya,** who is considered as the embodiment of the divine feminine power.
 
• The temple holds great religious significance and is one of the oldest and most revered **Shakti peethas** (sacred sites associated with the goddess Shakti) in India.
 
• It attracts a large number of devotees and pilgrims from all over the country.
 
• The architecture of the Kamakhya Temple reflects a unique blend of both Hindu and indigenous architectural styles.
 
• The main temple structure features a **dome-like structure known as the shikhara**, which is adorned with intricate sculptures and carvings.
 
• The temple complex comprises several other smaller temples dedicated to different deities.
 
• One of the notable rituals associated with the Kamakhya Temple is the **Ambubachi Mela,** which is celebrated annually during the monsoon season.
 
• It is believed that during this time, the goddess Kamakhya undergoes her menstrual cycle, and the temple remains closed for three days.
 
• The doors are reopened on the fourth day, and devotees gather to receive the blessings of the goddess.
 
• The Kamakhya Temple not only serves as a religious and spiritual center but also stands as a significant cultural landmark in the region.
 
• 
 
Its picturesque location atop the hill provides panoramic views of the city of Guwahati and the surrounding natural beauty.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Kamakhya Temple__.

questions.question: How many pairs of autosomes does a normal human have?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**22**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **No. of Chromosome in Humans**

 
 
• The nucleus of every cell contains microscopic, thread-like components that make up a **chromosome**.
 
• Each chromosome is made up **structurally of DNA **that is tightly wound around distinct proteins known as histones.
 
• There are **46 chromosomes** in all, divided into **23 pairs** in humans.
 
• These **22 pairs**—which are the same for both males and females—are referred to as the **autosomes**.
 
• There are differences between the sexes in the** 23rd pair of chromosomes**, or** "allosomes," which is the sex chromosome**.
 
• When compared to **females**, who have two copies of the "X" chromosome **(44A + XX)**, **males** only have one "X" and one "Y" chromosome **(44A+ XY)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Except for sex determination, autosomes are primarily linked to the **numerous metabolic processes that occur within the cell**.
 
• It occurs **half in no. in sex cells (gametes) and in pairs in somatic cells**.
 
• In humans, each parent gives one of their sex chromosomes to the child, dividing the child's chromosomes **equally between the mother and the father**.
 
• **DNA** is stored in a cell's chromosomes, which also have components needed for **segregation and replication**.

questions.question: As per Census 2011, which state of India has the highest sex ratio?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Kerala.__ 

__
 
• In 2011, male to female ratio for Kerala was 1,084 females per 1,000 males.
 
• People in Kerala are well educated, hence there is little distinction between a female and a boy. As a result, there is no female feticide and the sex ratio is balanced.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• The number of women and men in a country is an important demographic characteristic.
 
• The ratio between the number of women and men in the population is called the Sex Ratio.
 
• In some countries it is calculated by using the formula:
 
 
• Male Population/ Female Population X 1000 or
 
• the number of males per thousand females.
 
 
 
• In India, the sex ratio is worked out using the formula:
 
 
• Female Population / Male Population × 1000 
 
• or the number of females per thousand males.
 
 
 
• The sex ratio is an important information about the status of women in a country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Male to female ratio of Kerala increased from 1,011 females per 1,000 males in 1921 to 1,084 females per 1,000 males in 2011 growing at an average annual rate of 0.78%. 
 
• Kerala has the most girls per man in India. According to the 2001 census, 1058 was one of the most popular in India.

Hence, the correct answer is Kerala has the highest sex ratio in India as per Census 2011.

questions.question: If unemployment continues for long-term in a country, it is called ______ unemployment.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chronic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chronic Unemployment:**

 
 
• Chronic unemployment refers to** long-term unemployment typically caused by structural problems in the economy.**
 
• It is not due to the usual ups and downs of the business cycle but rather persists even in good economic times.
 
• Those who suffer from **chronic unemployment lack the skills or education needed for new jobs or live in parts of the country where jobs are scarce.**
 
• This type of unemployment can lead to a vicious cycle of** joblessness, poverty, and social issues.**
 
• It requires concerted policy efforts to resolve, such as** retraining programs, education reform, and economic development initiatives.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Casual Unemployment:**

 
 
• This refers to temporary **unemployment which occurs when workers are laid off or lose their jobs due to seasonal changes in demand or supply in certain industries.**
 
 
 
• **Technological Unemployment:**
 
 
• This type of unemployment is caused by **technological changes or automation that render certain jobs obsolete.**
 
• Workers displaced by technology **need to acquire new skills to find employment in other sectors.**
 
 
 
• **Frictional Unemployment:**
 
 
• This is a type of **short-term unemployment that occurs when people are between jobs or are looking for their first job.**
 
• **It's a natural part of the job market as people move between roles and careers.**

• The agriculture** sector**__ faces the problem of seasonal unemployment.
 
• ​Seasonal unemployment is unemployment that occurs during a certain season of the year.
 
 
• **Unemployment of the farmers during the non-crop season is an example of seasonal unemployment.**
 
• It is a common form of unemployment in rural areas.
 
• Unemployment rate = (Unemployed Workers / Total labour force) × 100
 
 
 
• The primary job of farmers is to sow and harvest rabi and Kharif crops.
 
 
• His source of income comes from selling crops.
 
• The time wherein there is no crop to sow or harvest or sell is the period when he is unemployed.

questions.question: What type of the rock is Granite?

__**Concept: **__

__
 
• A **rock** is any **naturally occurring solid mass or aggregate of one or more minerals** or mineraloid matter.
 
• The earth's **crust is composed of rocks.**
 
• It is categorized by the **minerals included its chemical composition **and the way in which it is formed.
 
• The rock cycle is a basic concept of transitions through geologic time among the three main rock types: **sedimentary, metamorphic, and igneous.**
 
• Each rock type is altered when it is forced out of its equilibrium conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Types of rocks**
 **Characteristics**
 
 

 **Igneous rock**
 
 
 
• It is formed when **molten rock (magma or lava) cools and solidifies.**
 
• Igneous rock may form with or without crystallization.
 
• It may be intrusive (plutonic) rocks or extrusive (volcanic) rocks.
 
• For example, **Granite, Basalt, etc.**
 

 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/974568e7db83f818a3567f7d2a635639513f30755928fc08e28ffed00807654f.png] ​

 
 
 

 **Sedimentary rock**
 
 
 
• They originate when **particles settle out of water or air, or by precipitation** of minerals from water.
 
• They accumulate in layers.
 
• For example, **Sandstone, Limestone, etc.**
 

 
**​** [IMAGE: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/Triassic_Utah.JPG/400px-Triassic_Utah.JPG] 

 
 
 

 **Metamorphic rock**
 
 
 
• They are formed when existing rocks are **changed by heat, pressure, or reactive fluids,** such as hot, mineral-laden water.
 
• For example, **Marble, Quartzite, Schist, etc.**
 

 
**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5beed19d56e85eabea71756d56469d93ed540284b346ff5f9075fbd3b5675f41.png]

questions.question: Article 45 under the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution, provides for

options.text: Rights of minorities to establish educational institutions
Education for weaker sections of the country
Giving financial assistance to less advanced states

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Free and compulsory primary education**__**.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• **Article 45 under Directive Principles of State Policy** laid down the foundation stone of **free and compulsory education in the country**. The article states that “** **the state shall endeavour to provide, within a period of ten years from the commencement of this constitution, for **free and compulsory education for all children until they complete the age of fourteen years**”. **Article 45 recognizes the child’s right to get an education and directs the state: **
 
• To make primary education compulsory and available to all;
 
• To encourage the development of different forms of secondary education, including general and vocational education, make them accessible and available to every child,** **and take appropriate measures such as the** **introduction of free education and offering financial assistance in case of need.
 
• Equality of educational** **opportunity** **can not be denied to anyone under **Article 29(2) **according to which **admission cannot be refused to anyone on the basis of race, caste, the language** in any institution maintained by the state or aided by the state.
 
• Also, the** five articles - 15, 29(2), 15(3), 46 and 29(l) **entrust the** responsibility of equalization of educational opportunity i**n all parts of the country to the Government of India and to that end, to give special assistance to backward areas or states.
 
• It is therefore clear that the task of** **providing universal educational opportunity to all children of the country is the **joint responsibility** of the central government, state governments, and local bodies as well as voluntary organizations.
 
• The central government, in respect of primary education, has some important roles to play such as initiating researches and pilot projects in elementary education, providing financial assistance to states, acting as a coordinating agency between state and other international agencies, and sorting out the differences between various states, ensuring equitable distribution of resources and inequality of opportunities, etc. 

**Hence, we conclude that Article 45 under the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution, provides for ​Free and compulsory primary education.**
